layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 17 congressional districts — the largest districts Pennsylvania carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (120th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 17 features for Pennsylvania, measured 2026-11-10. Layer 4, the 119th Congress's map, draws the same 17 districts (lowest district IoU 1.0), because Pennsylvania's map is still the one the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania adopted in February 2022, so nothing changes on 3 January 2027 and the builder refuses to write if the two differ before then. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: Pennsylvania Senate District
layers.rank_note: 50 Senate districts — larger on average than a county, smaller than a congressional district

source.answers: The Pennsylvania Senate district covering the point, and the senator holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 1 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Upper), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 50 features, measured 2026-11-10: the 2022 plan of the Legislative Reapportionment Commission, which the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania upheld that year. Layer 5, the 2024 districts, agrees district for district (lowest district IoU 0.99986, District 22). Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: pa-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the General Assembly's own member list and each senator's page at palegis.us: name, party, Capitol office, its mailing address and telephone, and the senator's e-mail address where the list prints one (36 of 50 on 2026-11-10; the others link a contact form).

layers.rank_note: 67 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 67 features, measured 2026-11-10. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Pennsylvania's counties elect commissioners, or a council and executive under a home rule charter, and row officers such as a sheriff and a district attorney, and no list of them was read in this pass; the card names the county only. Recorded as gap pa-county-officials.

layers.label: School District
layers.rank_note: 500 school districts, every one unified, plus the Census placeholder for Lake Erie, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The public school district covering the point.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 0 (unified school districts), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 501 features for Pennsylvania, measured 2026-11-10: 500 districts and the record the Census names School District Not Defined, GEOID 4299997, which is Pennsylvania's part of Lake Erie (no land) and which the card answers as the lake. The elementary and secondary layers carry nothing for Pennsylvania, whose 500 school districts each run every grade.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Each district's board of school directors is elected, and no statewide list of them was read in this pass — recorded as gap pa-school-board-members.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: 2,382 ZIP Code Tabulation Areas in the state's own bounding box, drawn from a tile archive of the ones inside Pennsylvania; the layer hides outside the state

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, mirrored into a vector-tile archive of the ZCTAs inside Pennsylvania (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py). ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='42'. 2,382 features in Pennsylvania's box, which reaches into the six neighbouring states, measured 2026-11-10.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: Pennsylvania. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code.

layers.label: City, Borough or Township
layers.rank_note: 2,567 municipalities (1,544 townships, 960 borough pieces, 56 city pieces, 6 home rule municipalities and the town of Bloomsburg), about 46 km2 on average, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The city, borough, township or town containing the point, and its county.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 1 (county subdivisions), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 2,568 features for Pennsylvania, measured 2026-11-10. EVERY PART OF PENNSYLVANIA'S LAND IS IN ONE MUNICIPALITY, and the Census files each city, borough and town as a county subdivision of its own beside the townships, so this one layer is the state's whole municipal map. A city or borough that crosses a county line is one feature in each county. One feature is not a municipality: Pennsylvania's part of Lake Erie, which the Census files as 'County subdivisions not defined' in Erie County, and the card treats it as water.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Pennsylvania's cities, boroughs, townships and towns elect their own officials, and no statewide roster of them was read in this pass; the card names the municipality and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap pa-municipal-officeholders.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-11-10: 1412 points in Pennsylvania's envelope, under the service's 2,000-record cap today, and paged anyway so that stops being a fact anyone has to re-check.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: Pennsylvania — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: Pennsylvania State Capitol, 501 North 3rd Street, Harrisburg, Dauphin County

negative_point.note: Lake Erie on the Canadian side of the international line, north of Erie — outside Pennsylvania and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-11-10: TIGERweb's state layer places it in no state (controls: the State Capitol returns Pennsylvania, and a point in the open Atlantic returns no state), none of the state's shipped boundary files contains it, and no outline in fleet-outlines.json does. IT IS WATER, SO NO NEIGHBOUR'S GO-LIVE MOVES IT.

The 67 counties — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The 17 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 0 (CD120), the 2022 map, the same map as layer 4.
The 50 Pennsylvania Senate districts, TIGERweb layer 1, the 2022 plan.
The 203 Pennsylvania House districts, TIGERweb layer 2, the 2022 plan.

The ZIP code search index (scripts/build_zip_index.mjs): one Point per ZIP code the app's ZIP layer draws, at the spot inside it on the layer's own ground farthest from every edge, with its extent and its layer, so a ZIP code typed into the search box selects that spot, turns the ZIP layer on and pins it for comparison (ENGINE geocoder-search, showZip). A ZIP code with no spot 75 m clear of every edge is left out, and one that crosses into another app's state is listed by whichever app holds more of it. GENERATED from data/app/tiles/zip-code.pmtiles, with each spot inside metro-outline.json (the outline its coverage test reads); --check rebuilds it from the committed archive and outline. Exact count, because it changes only when the Census Bureau changes its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and that wants reading rather than a widened bound.

The officers Pennsylvania elects statewide and its two U.S. senators: state, officers (office, name, the office's own website, the day the name was last checked there) and usSenate. Built weekly by scripts/build_statewide_officials.py from pa/data/source/statewide-officials.source.json, which lists each office, the name and the page that must print it; the build reads robots.txt before every page, refuses to write when a page it read no longer prints the name, keeps the last checked record when a page cannot be read, and takes the senators from senate.gov's own list. Network-first: a name can change.
